sonnet.problem: Card 10 says 'Now the LORD speaks' for Micah 1:6 ('I will make Samaria a heap of rubble…'). The text never says who is speaking here. v5 and v8 are also spoken as 'I' with no speaker named, so the card guesses.
sonnet.rule: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first. … When the text doesn't say who is speaking, he doesn't guess. He uses a plain lead-in, like "Then the psalm says…", and names a speaker only when the passage or its heading does.

sonnet.problem: Card 13 quotes v7 and attributes it to 'the LORD says'. v7 is an 'I' statement ('I will destroy all her idols') and the text names no speaker.
sonnet.rule: When the text doesn't say who is speaking, he doesn't guess. He uses a plain lead-in, like "Then the psalm says…", and names a speaker only when the passage or its heading does.

sonnet.problem: Card 15 says 'Micah says he'll walk barefoot and naked…' for v8 ('I will lament and wail; I will walk barefoot…'). The text does not name the speaker of this 'I', so the card guesses.
sonnet.rule: When the text doesn't say who is speaking, he doesn't guess. He uses a plain lead-in, like "Then the psalm says…", and names a speaker only when the passage or its heading does.

sonnet.problem: The statement says Micah laments 'Because of what's coming for Samaria'. v8 says only 'Because of this', and the text does not say what 'this' is or who is speaking. The card closes that gap itself.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The valleys splitting in v4 was never told on an earlier card. Card 6 covers only the mountains. A baker can only guess whether the valleys 'hold firm', so a 50/50 true/false pick comes down to luck.
sonnet.rule: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
